svg.title: To recover cover coefficients from these all-period limits, take two possible coefficient limits R, R′ of a uniformly exponentially bounded row. Their folded kernels agree on every scheduled torus. Fix a cover displacement z and choose a torus whose centered box contains z. The folded coefficient at its residue is R(z) plus the other congruent coefficients. Their sum is bounded by a constant times the exponential tail outside that box, uniformly in the history index. As the scheduled periods grow, this tail tends to zero, hence R(z) = R′(z). Compact coefficient extraction therefore has only one possible limit; the full row converges coefficientwise. Splitting into a finite displacement set and its exponentially bounded complement proves convergence in every strictly smaller strip norm, exactly as in (SH2)–(SH3). The argument applies to the diagonal, its dual and the amended metric. The physical covariance and response rows have in addition the rate (SH9).
